scenes.headline: How Jina-OCR-v1 turns a page into Markdown
scenes.sub: DeepSeek-OCR's encoder and decoder, plus one shared block that drafts ahead.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jasper! Jina-OCR-v1 reads a document page and writes it out as Markdown. Here's what's inside, and the one part that's new.

scenes.text: Jina-OCR-v1 is DeepSeek-OCR plus one new part: a single draft block, run three times, that guesses tokens for the decoder to check.
scenes.say: Almost everything here is DeepSeek-OCR's design. The new part is one small block that guesses the next three tokens for the decoder to check.

steps.say: A page goes in at a thousand twenty-four pixels square. DeepEncoder compresses it sixteen times between two vision encoders.
That leaves two hundred fifty-six tokens for the page, plus up to nine tiles of a hundred. It runs once per page.
A twelve-layer mixture-of-experts decoder writes Markdown. Each token uses six of sixty-four routed experts, plus two shared.
The new part: a FastMTP draft block reads the decoder's hidden state and guesses ahead.

items.say: It takes the decoder's hidden state and guesses the next token.
It feeds its guess back through the same block, three times.
The decoder verifies the drafts greedily.
It keeps the longest run greedy decoding would have produced anyway, so the output is unchanged.

scenes.label: active decoder parameters per token, summed from the shipped tensors; 570M advertised
scenes.note: embedding and output head are two matrices, not one tied
scenes.say: Count what runs per token from the shipped tensors: about seven hundred forty million, not five-seventy. The embedding and output head aren't tied.

scenes.text: Drafting ahead never changes the output, but its payoff depends on the baseline: under CUDA graphs, one draft beats three.
scenes.say: So drafting ahead never changes the output. But its payoff depends on the baseline: nearly double in eager PyTorch, and under CUDA graphs, one draft beats three.

recap: DeepEncoder turns a page into at most 1,156 tokens
A MoE decoder writes Markdown, six of 64 experts
One shared block drafts three tokens, losslessly
scenes.say: To recap: a compressed page, a sparse decoder, and one small block that drafts ahead without changing a word.
